headline: Actress Azmeri Haque Badhan assaulted and harassed in Italy, files police complaint
summary: Bangladeshi actress Azmeri Haque Badhan was pelted with water, soft drinks, and eggs, and physically assaulted while with her family in Venice. She alleges the attack was politically motivated due to her support for the student movement.
details: Noted actress Azmeri Haque Badhan was attacked and harassed in Italy while spending time with her brother and his family. She reported being pelted with water, soft drinks, and eggs, and physically assaulted during the incident.

Badhan, who is in Venice for the premiere of her film "The Difficult Bride", stated her mobile phone was knocked out of her hand and she was struck near her ear. Her brother’s young child was also present, and she has since filed a complaint with local police.

The "Rehana Maryam Noor" actress alleges she was targeted because of her active role in the July-August 2024 student-led mass movement. She had publicly spoken out against attacks on students and supported the movement to both local and international media.

According to Badhan, some of the attackers identified themselves as members of the Awami League and Bangladesh Chhatra League, both of which are banned. Some also claimed to be “soldiers of Bangabandhu” and reportedly forced her to say, “Joy Bangla, Joy Bangabandhu”.

The attackers allegedly attempted to record the incident and livestream the footage on social media. Videos later shared by Badhan show people calling her a “July militant” and making aggressive remarks about her political views.

Badhan’s brother’s wife was also pushed during the incident. Condemning the attack, Badhan stated, “It will not be so easy to silence Azmeri Haque Badhan. Today, you have shown people around the world how an actress representing Bangladesh was harassed.”
In her video message, Badhan also mentioned learning that Sajeeb Wazed Joy, son of the ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, was in Venice. She urged that the incident be brought to his attention.

topic: UN Human Rights Chief on Bangladesh law enforcement
headline_marked: UN Chief [[independent body to monitor law enforcement]] in Bangladesh
headline: UN Chief independent body to monitor law enforcement in Bangladesh
summary: UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk calls for accountability and oversight of security forces following July-August protests.
details: UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk has called for the creation of a strong and independent national institution to monitor Bangladesh's law enforcement agencies.

Speaking at the 63rd session of the UN Human Rights Council in Geneva on Monday, Türk emphasized the need for effective oversight and accountability to ensure law enforcement agencies operate within the law.

This call follows a UN report on human rights violations during the July-August 2024 protests, which provided 44 recommendations, including independent investigations into allegations against security forces.
The report also stressed the importance of civilian oversight and empowering the National Human Rights Commission to be more effective in its role.
Additionally, Türk addressed the human rights situation in Myanmar, noting that the Rohingya conflict has had a severe adverse impact on neighboring countries, particularly Bangladesh.
He stated that the Rohingya crisis is the result of widespread and systematic human rights violations in Rakhine, including arbitrary arrests, persecution, and forced displacement.
Türk attributed the current instability in Rakhine to the actions of both the Myanmar military and the Arakan Army.

The UN is calling for a strong, independent body to hold Bangladesh's security forces accountable.

This call follows a UN report on human rights violations during the July-August 2024 protests, which provided 44 recommendations, including independent investigations into allegations against security forces.

Additionally, Türk addressed the human rights situation in Myanmar, noting that the Rohingya conflict has had a severe adverse impact on neighboring countries, particularly Bangladesh.
